question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
sql:
-- Check customer 312's March 1-12 balances
WITH daily_amounts AS (
    SELECT customer_id, txn_date, 
           SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount 
                    WHEN txn_type = 'purchase' THEN -txn_amount 
                    WHEN txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount 
                    ELSE 0 END) as daily_net
    FROM customer_transactions 
    WHERE customer_id = 312
    GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
customer_ranges AS (
    SELECT customer_id, 
           CAST(MIN(txn_date) AS DATE) as min_date, 
           CAST(MAX(txn_date) AS DATE) as max_date
    FROM customer_transactions 
    WHERE customer_id = 312
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
date_series AS (
    SELECT customer_id, 
           CAST(DATE_ADD(min_date, INTERVAL (n) DAY) AS DATE) as cal_date
    FROM customer_ranges, 
         LATERAL (SELECT UNNEST(GENERATE_SERIES(0, DATEDIFF('day', min_date, max_date))) AS n)
),
filled_daily AS (
    SELECT ds.customer_id, ds.cal_date, COALESCE(da.daily_net, 0) as daily_net
    FROM date_series ds
    LEFT JOIN daily_amounts da ON ds.customer_id = da.customer_id AND CAST(da.txn_date AS DATE) = ds.cal_date
),
with_balance AS (
    SELECT customer_id, cal_date, daily_net,
           SUM(daily_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY cal_date) as running_balance
    FROM filled_daily
),
clamped AS (
    SELECT customer_id, cal_date, 
           GREATEST(running_balance, 0) as daily_balance
    FROM with_balance
)
SELECT cal_date, daily_balance
FROM clamped
WHERE cal_date >= '2020-03-01' AND cal_date <= '2020-03-15'
ORDER BY cal_date
